title: Transfer latest: Konsa, Jones & Baleba updates plus reporter Q&A
author: Live Reporting Written by Emma Smith; Flora Snelson; Tasnim Chowdhury; Grace Wheeler
content:
![](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/128/cpsprodpb//vivo/live/images/2026/6/11/58b52225-f56a-4b3b-bd61-1f10dfd2100e.jpg.webp) Dale Johnson
Football issues correspondent
Kieran, Omagh: What is the latest in which a club can register a new signing ahead of their opening game of the season?
Players must be registered before 12:00 on the last working day before the match.
However, do not be too concerned if the clock ticks past noon on Friday and the new signing has been announced.
Quite often a deal will be completed, but the club still needs to get the photoshops and interviews done to put up as part of the announcement.
So sometimes a transfer might be announced in the afternoon, but the player will actually have been registered ahead of the deadline.
summary: Football clubs must register new signings by 12:00 on the last working day before their opening match. However, clubs often complete the registration before the deadline while delaying the public announcement to finish promotional photos and interviews. Therefore, an afternoon announcement does not necessarily mean the player missed the registration cutoff.
key_points: Players must be registered before noon on the last working day prior to a match.
Announcements are sometimes delayed past the registration deadline for media purposes.
A player can be officially registered even if their club announces the transfer in the afternoon.

title: Transfer news LIVE: Man Utd in Baleba breakthrough, Arsenal agree Konsa deal
author: Miguel Delaney; Jack Rathborn; Harry Latham-Coyle
content:
Manchester United are closing in on a third centre-midfield signing of the summer and have made a £60m bid for Carlos Baleba with the Brighton player expected to move to Old Trafford. United have tracked the Cameroon international for some time and could improve their offer by £5m, with the player first targeted last summer. Back then, Brighton valued the 22-year-old at over £100m, but after a difficult year, United appear to have struck a deal at a more attractive fee.
Elsewhere, Liverpool have entered into negotiations with Inter Milan about selling Curtis Jones to the Italian champions. The two clubs are yet to agree a deal but dialogue is ongoing as Inter have resumed their attempts to buy the midfielder. Liverpool would probably agree to a sum of around €35m (£30m) to let Jones move to San Siro. The Reds remani interested in Bradley Barcola after dropping their pursuit of his PSG’s team-mate Ibrahim Mbaye.
Meanwhile, Arsenal have agreed to sign Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa for around £51m. Mikel Arteta was eager to bolster his defence after the serious injury to William Saliba and Jurrien Timber’s return to fitness and a right-sided defender was highlighted as a priority for the Gunners as they bid to defend their Premier League title. The 28-year-old would likely compete with Cristhian Mosquera to deputise for Saliba alongside Gabriel Magalhaes and could make his debut against Aston Villa next week.
Finally, Tottenham are interested in Omar Marmoush as well as Savinho as they could make two signings from Manchester City. Savinho is a long-term target for Spurs, who considered a £50m move for the Brazilian winger last summer. But they are also keen on Marmoush as Roberto De Zerbi looks to strengthen his forward line and continue his expensive revamp of a squad who only just avoided relegation last season.
Follow all of the latest news, rumours and done deals below
Hull accelerate talks for Real Betis winger
Hull City are hoping to boost their survival hopes a deal progressing nicely for Real Betis winger Pablo Garcia.
The 20-year-old is a target for the Tigers, reports Sport in Spain.
The Under-21 international broke through last season for the Seville-based club and has three goals in five caps for that age bracket.
Liam Delap training separately to Chelsea squad
Could Liam Delap leave Chelsea? There is a bit of a striking logjam at the club for Xabi Alonso to sort out, and it appears last year’s signing is among a group of players training away from the first-team squad. He has also lost the No 9 shirt – ominous....
Everton track Como starlet
The Senegal star might cost in the region of £50-60m.
The 20-year-old arrived in Italy from Real Betis last year and scored twice in 17 Serie A appearances under Cesc Fabregas.
Diao featured in the 5-0 win over Iraq for Senegal at the World Cup this summer.
Why Carlos Baleba could be the missing piece in Manchester United’s new midfield
As reported earlier, Manchester United are closing in on a deal to sign Carlos Baleba from Brighton. Lawrence Ostlere explains how the midfielder will fit in with Michael Carrick’s side – and why he could be just what they need...
Barcelona put move for Julian Alvarez on hold?
It had been presumed that Julian Alvarez was bound for Barcelona after Atletico Madrid exiled the striker from their squad – but reports in Spain suggest the Catalan club are pursuing other targets. ESPN suggests that frustration has grown over Atletico’s unwillingness to sell, which could force the champions to look elsewhere.
![Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez](https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/06/09/19/00e50537ccd47122ec6510357cdbc1f7Y29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzgxMTEzNDc2-2.84456868.jpg)
Serie A giants line up for United striker
As Manchester United's look to bolster their squad with Carlos Baleba’s prospective arrival, there could be exits, starting with Joshua Zirkzee.
The Netherlands forward, 25, could return to Italy, where he shone for Bologna.
And Gazzetta dello Sport reports that Juventus and Napoli retain an interest. United would look to recoup the £36.5m they paid Bologna in 2024.
![Joshua Zirkzee celebrates with Manchester United teammates Bryan Mbeumo](https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/08/12/21/0c3dc0e88f1f765bac7c4b819f2a7a83Y29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzg2NjUxMjE5-2.85546503.jpg)
Sunderland to break club record for Sporting star?
Sunderland are looking into a mega move for Sporting Lisbon winger Geny Catamo, reports Teamtalk.
The Black Cats would need to trigger the Mozambique star’s €60m (£51m) release clause.
Catamo scored seven goals last term, adding three assists and would bring another threat to Regis Le Bris’ side.
Kane on Barcelona's radar with Bayern future unclear
Barcelona are looking into Harry Kane's situation amid contract talks with Bayern Munich.
The Mail reports that the England striker, 33, is on Barcelona’s radar with just one year left on his contract at the Allianz Arena.
Kane has also been linked with a move to Saudi Pro League's Al-Hilal, though he has maintained he is content with life in the Bundesliga.
The England forward is the favourite to win the Ballon d’Or with the bookmakers after a staggering 50-goal campaign for the Bavarian giants.
![](https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/08/18/16/01M0AJH2XSRJFT0DM3NDFQD8XQ.jpg)
Villa target Chelsea defender as Konsa replacement
With Ezri Konsa set for Arsenal, Aston Villa are looking to fill the gap and their familiar relationship with Chelsea could prove handy.
Tosin Adarabioyo is on their radar, reports Sky Sports, while Benfica are also keen on the English defender, add The Sun.
Chelsea could move a second play to Villa Park, though it would need to be a permanent deal, given Alejandro Garnacho has joined on an initial loan deal from the club.
![Tosin could leave Chelsea this summer](https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/01/10/23/287389bdb92d7c2e8377ea1e9888910fY29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzY4MTczNjEz-2.83008102.jpg)
Manchester United table bid for Carlos Baleba as midfield rebuild continues
Manchester United have made a £60m bid for Carlos Baleba as they look to make the Brighton player their third midfield signing of the summer.
They are yet to agree a deal, with Brighton thought to want a higher price for the Cameroon international, but talks are progressing.
summary: Manchester United have made a £60m bid to sign Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba. Meanwhile, Arsenal have agreed a deal to sign Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa for approximately £51m following an injury to William Saliba. Additionally, Liverpool are in talks with Inter Milan regarding the potential sale of midfielder Curtis Jones for around £30m.
key_points: Manchester United have submitted a £60m bid for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba.
Arsenal have agreed to sign Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa for about £51m.
Liverpool and Inter Milan are in ongoing negotiations over a £30m move for Curtis Jones.
Aston Villa have targeted Chelsea's Tosin Adarabioyo as a potential replacement for Konsa.

title: Formula 1: Max Verstappen extends deal with Red Bull to 2030
author: Andrew Benson
content:
![Max Verstappen in a black Red Bull racing outfit](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/819/cpsprodpb/c891/live/b9546870-9c66-11f1-827b-69a6492daae1.jpg)
Max Verstappen best results this season have been two second places
- Published
Four-time world champion Max Verstappen has signed a new contract at Red Bull until the end of 2030.
The move should end speculation about the Dutchman's future at the end of this season, after he had been linked with potential moves to Mercedes or McLaren.
Verstappen was previously contracted to the end of 2028, but there were clauses in his contract that would have allowed him to leave at the end of the current Formula 1 season had he wanted.
"We have the best people and I'm excited to keep working together with everyone to get back to the top again," said Verstappen, 28.
"This remains the ultimate goal that all of us have been working towards and will continue to pursue.
"I have always said it: the team is like a second family for me and I feel very at home.
"I came to the team hoping to be able to win races. What we went on to achieve together has been simply lovely and we have shared many incredible moments and won four World Championships.
"To continue this journey with the same team that I have been with my whole career is really special and something I have always wanted to do."
Red Bull have had a difficult start to the era of new regulations for cars and engines introduced for this season.
Verstappen's best results have been two second places, in the Austrian and Hungarian Grands Prix, after coming within two points of beating McLaren's Lando Norris to the world title last season. That 2025 close call followed a dramatic fightback in the second half of the season from a deficit of more than 100 points to the championship lead.
Red Bull's lack of performance has led to Verstappen voicing frustration on a number of occasions, but in the end he has decided to stick with what he knows.
The decision comes despite his trusted race engineer Gianpiero Lambiase signing to join McLaren by 2028.
Verstappen's renewal statement included praise for team principal Laurent Mekies, who took over last July after former boss Christian Horner was sacked following a turbulent 18-month period and a decline in competitiveness.
"Getting to work with Laurent now for over a year has also been great, I see a clear vision he has for the team," Verstappen said.
"Everyone [at Red Bull's base] in Milton Keynes believes in what we are building and I am looking forward to the next chapter, fighting for more victories and competing for championships as we continue to shape the future of this team."
The announcement has been timed to coincide with Verstappen's final home race this weekend before the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort falls off the calendar.
![Max Verstappen and Laurent Mekies](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1008/cpsprodpb/1388/live/3ba92a30-9c68-11f1-827b-69a6492daae1.jpg)
Max Verstappen signs his new contract alongside team principal Laurent Mekies
Although the deal takes Verstappen to the end of 2030, there are still mechanisms by which he could leave if performance does not come up to expectations.
This is standard practice in driver contracts in F1. The details are not yet known, and teams do not comment on contractual intricacies.
Mekies said: "Having Max continue with us and retaining the best driver on the grid is fantastic news.
"Very few partnerships in sport achieve what Max and this team have. Since the very beginning, Max has embodied everything that makes Red Bull Racing special: uncompromising competitiveness, relentless determination and the courage to challenge convention.
"His impact on our team and Red Bull's motorsport story has been transformational and he has been fundamental to everything we have achieved together.
"The decision to continue our journey together is rooted in the trust Max and the team have built over many years, as well as Max's confidence in our people, our culture and our vision for the future.
"Forged through championship-winning success, intense battles and challenging moments alike, this relationship has only grown stronger â making it one of Formula 1's greatest success stories. But we are not done yet. There are more races to win, more milestones to achieve and more history to write."
Verstappen started his F1 career with Red Bull's junior team, then called Toro Rosso, in 2015. He was promoted to the senior team after four races of his second season, 2016, and immediately won his first race.
He has since gone on to win 71 grands prix alongside his four world titles, with his tally of race victories ranking third in all-time F1 history after Lewis Hamilton and Michael Schumacher.
summary: Four-time Formula 1 world champion Max Verstappen has signed a contract extension with Red Bull through the end of 2030, ending speculation about a potential move to Mercedes or McLaren. Despite Red Bull facing a challenging start under new car and engine regulations, Verstappen expressed confidence in team principal Laurent Mekies and the team's vision. The new deal includes standard mechanisms that would still allow Verstappen to leave if performance does not meet expectations.
key_points: Max Verstappen extended his Red Bull contract to the end of 2030, previously being bound until 2028 with exit clauses.
The 28-year-old driver has won four world titles and 71 grands prix during his career with Red Bull.
Red Bull experienced a difficult start to the new regulations era, with Verstappen's best results this season being two second-place finishes.
Verstappen praised the clear vision of team principal Laurent Mekies, who took over last July after Christian Horner was sacked.
The contract extension features standard F1 mechanisms allowing potential departure if performance targets are not met.

title: Barcola to Liverpool deal will 'be done this week' as Collymore labels star a 'massive upgrade' on 'six out of 10' star
author: James Marshment
content:
![Liverpool](https://www.teamtalk.com/content/themes/teamtalk2/img/png/team-icon/LIV.png) 
![PSG star Bradley Barcola is Liverpool's top summer target PSG star Bradley Barcola next to the Liverpool badge](https://images.teamtalk.com/content/uploads/2026/08/19144217/PSG-star-Bradley-Barcola-is-Liverpools-top-summer-target.jpg) 
Liverpool are growing in confidence that a deal for Bradley Barcola will soon be finalised, with one well-informed journalist suggesting a deal could be done this week, while the PSG star has been branded a game-changing addition for Andoni Iraola and a major upgrade on Cody Gakpo.
The Reds are strongly pushing to bring in Barcola as the marquee addition to their attack, with Liverpool seeking a high-calibre replacement for Mohamed Salah.
Striking a deal, though, with PSG will not be easy, and despite our revelation that Luis Enrique has decided to freeze the player out of their first-team plans until a resolution is found, the European champions are demanding a hefty fee for the 23-year-old star.
Indeed, with talks ongoing over a potential deal, Liverpool could be looking at forking out a fee in excess of £115m (€135m, $157m) for the 28-cap France attacker.
Despite the sky-high fees involved, his prospective signing has been welcomed by Stan Collymore, who has exclusively told TEAMtalk why the addition of Barcola can help Iraola’s side reach the next level.
“He represents a clear upgrade on Gakpo,” Collymore told us in association with 10bet, the home of football betting. “When I look at Gakpo, I see a central striker who has been shunted out to the left. He’s done fine and scored goals from there, but he’s essentially an awkward striker adapted to play on the left of a front three.
“Barcola, on the other hand, can play down either flank or drop off as a number 10 because he carries the ball well, beats defenders, and creates chances. He has that sharp, sliding pass to set up teammates.
“In a market where Morgan Rogers and Elliot Anderson go for record fees and top game-changers command £115m to £116m, paying that extra amount for a player of Barcola’s profile isn’t a massive stretch.
“He’s a staple in the French national team. Having a player who can pick up the ball on the edge of the 18-yard box, slide throughballs to Isak, or beat his man on the outside to whip low crosses across the six-yard box would be a massive asset for Liverpool.”
DON’T MISS: Barcola’s Liverpool transfer dream laid bare as Reds ready gigantic second offer
Liverpool’s Barcola signing to go through this week – journalist
Collymore also explained why he thinks the time has come for Liverpool to move Gakpo on, with the Dutchman the subject of interest from Tottenham Hotspur.
“Liverpool fans and the club would likely say they got decent value for what they paid. He wasn’t spectacular. Over his tenure, he’s been a six-and-a-half out of ten, who scored big goals in key moments.
“However, as a central number nine or on the left wing, his ceiling is somewhat limited. He has plateaued around the level he arrived at – a reliable six-and-a-half or seven out of ten max.
“Liverpool got what they paid for, whereas a player like Barcola offers the potential to consistently hit an eight or nine out of ten and be a true match-winner.
“In a league where Manchester City, Arsenal, Chelsea, and Aston Villa continue to invest heavily, match-winners in top-six clashes define where the title goes. Gakpo wasn’t that player, but Barcola certainly can be!”
Earlier this week, David Lynch revealed his optimism that a move to take Barcola to Anfield was now a question of ‘when, not if’, outlining his belief a deal was closing in.
Now, taking that to the next level, the Daily Mail’s Lewis Steele has suggested that an agreement between the clubs could be finalised ‘this week’.
He told Anfield Index’s YouTube channel: “I think that it’s going to be this week. It’s got to be this week!
“All the noise suggests that a second bid or a more official proposal and for the clubs to sort of meet in the middle is something that may happen.
“We know everyone in all parties desire is to make a move happen.”
“The worry is that the clock is ticking and they just need to get moving.”
On a potential timescale, he added: “Hopefully it’ll be for the second game.
“Liverpool have been after this fabled winger for what feels like five years now.”
In conclusion, he added: “Let’s just see what happens in the next 48 hours. But I think it’ll start moving soon.”
The good news for Liverpool is that personal terms for Barcola have already been agreed on a multi-year contract at Anfield.
Former Arsenal star Emmanuel Petit also thinks Barcola is Anfield-bound, explaining why the Reds will beat Arsenal to his signature.
summary: Liverpool are increasingly confident that a deal to sign PSG star Bradley Barcola could be finalized this week. The Reds are pursuing the 23-year-old France attacker as a marquee addition and a high-calibre replacement for Mohamed Salah, with potential fees exceeding £115m. Pundit Stan Collymore has endorsed the transfer, describing Barcola as a major upgrade on Cody Gakpo, while journalist Lewis Steele suggests an agreement between the clubs may happen imminently.
key_points: Liverpool are growing confident that a deal for PSG winger Bradley Barcola could be finalized this week.
The prospective transfer fee for the 23-year-old French international is expected to exceed £115m.
Former player Stan Collymore stated that Barcola represents a massive upgrade on Cody Gakpo.
Personal terms on a multi-year contract have already been agreed upon between Liverpool and Barcola.

title: ‘You don’t have many halves’: Robinson and Tongue split cricket ball after heroics
author: Taha Hashim
content:
A ball cut in half was the solution to Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue’s novel problem. Courtesy of a helpful member of the Headingley ground staff, the two quicks shared the souvenir after each took five wickets on the opening day of England’s first Test against Pakistan, with the visitors bowled out for 171.
“You don’t really have too many halves of cricket balls, so it’ll be something that we never forget,” said Robinson, showing off his share in his post-match press conference as he reflected on his haul of five for 51, including a wicket with the first ball of the series.
England find themselves in a commanding position as they begin life again under Joe Root’s captaincy, closing day one on 112 for two.
For Robinson it marked his first Test since featuring against New Zealand at Lord’s, which was his comeback match after two years in exile.
A knee problem ruled him out of the second Test of that series, and he was left out at Trent Bridge for Ben Stokes’ final hurrah. England lost both matches, and the series.
“It was frustrating not to be able to play at the Oval,” said Robinson. “Just a bit of a freak training injury and then I was available for Trent Bridge but not selected, and I suppose that’s part of professional sport, isn’t it?
after newsletter promotion
![Ollie Robinson holds up his half of the match ball after day one of the first Test between England and Pakistan.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/72f9d86664ac75cf6f5b8201449df325c9d52758/0_0_2093_2708/master/2093.jpg?width=120&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
“Since then I’ve just worked really hard on a bit more fitness and a bit more skill so it’s nice when it comes off on days like today. I probably learned a lot about myself when I was out of the team. At the moment I probably feel as good as I’ve ever felt.
“I’m probably not in as good a rhythm – and that sounds silly after [taking] wickets – but I’m probably not in as good a rhythm as I would like, having not played red-ball cricket since Lord’s. For me, the more I play, the better I tend to get. So as long as I can stay on the park and stay fit, hopefully I can get that rhythm.”
While Robinson and Tongue shared the wickets, the former was keen to big up England’s wider seam stocks, with Jofra Archer and Gus Atkinson forming their quartet for this Test.
“The four guys that played today – it’s a really exciting time for English cricket. You’ve got a few other lads in the background that can also come in and do the same job. I can’t remember a time in English cricket where you’ve got seven, eight, fit fast bowlers to choose from for a series.”
summary: Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue shared a cut cricket ball as a souvenir after each taking five wickets to bowl Pakistan out for 171 on the opening day of the first Test at Headingley. England finished the day in a commanding position at 112 for two under Joe Root's captaincy. The performance marked a strong return for Robinson following a period out of the team due to injury and non-selection.
key_points: Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue each took five wickets as Pakistan was bowled out for 171.
A member of the Headingley ground staff cut the match ball in half so the two bowlers could share the souvenir.
England closed the opening day of the Test in a commanding position at 112 for two.
Robinson returned to the team after missing recent matches due to a knee injury and non-selection.

title: Celtic 3-0 LASK: Camilo Duran nets stunning double as Hoops edge towards Champions League return
author: Alison Conroy
content:
Celtic 3-0 LASK: Camilo Duran nets stunning double as Hoops edge towards Champions League return
Report as Celtic beat LASK 3-0 in the first leg of their Champions League play-off; Benjamin Nygren opened the scoring and Camilo Duran netted a double; the visitors had two goals disallowed; the sides meet again on Tuesday
Wednesday 19 August 2026 22:54, UK
Celtic took a huge step towards a return to the Champions League with stunning goals from Benjamin Nygren and Camilo Duran.
After crashing out in the play-off round 12 months ago, it was almost a nightmare start when Moses Usor fired into the Celtic's net just seconds after kick-off. But the Hoops were saved by the offside flag.
They survived another scare before Nygren set the Hoops on their way, when he curled Kieran Tierney's ball into the top corner.

Samuel Adeniran also denied by the offside flag before Duran smashed Tierney's cross into the net for his first Parkhead goal.
It was an impressive strike, but there was better to come from the Colombian striker as he sidefooted into the far corner after a one-two with the club's other big summer arrival, Kasper Hogh.
The pair, who scored 10 Champions League goals between them last season, proving their worth in green and white early in the season.
Three up, but far from over. The Austrian champions carried plenty of threat as they try to reach Europe's top-tier competition for the first time.
The sides meet again in Linz on Tuesday. Can Martin O'Neill's side finish the job?
The key moments from Celtic Park
1: LASK SCORE EARLY BUT IT'S DISALLOWED! Usor fires into the top right corner, but the celebrations are cut short by the offside flag.
3: ANOTHER BIG CHANCE! Adeniran gets away from Carter-Vickers, races through on goal, but drags his shot wide.
9: FIRST CHANCE FOR CELTIC! Duran turns and hits it first time, but Jungwirth gets down to make the stop.
27: GOAL CELTIC! Tierney's ball falls into the path of Nygren, who curls his first-time effort into the top right corner.
35: LASK SCORE BUT IT'S DISALLOWED AGAIN! Adeniran heads into the bottom corner, but he's offside.
38: GOAL CELTIC! LASK clear Tierney's cross, but it falls to Duran outside the area and he smashes it into the net.
51: SAVE! Baur's ambitious volley from outside the area is straight at Jungwirth.
56: OFF THE POST! McGregor shoots from range and it takes a deflection off Hogh before hitting the woodwork.
62: BIG SAVE! Usor is denied by Sinisalo from point-blank range! Another chance squandered by LASK.
67: GOAL CELTIC! Another stunner! A sweeping counterattack ends with Duran combining with Nygren before guiding the ball into the net.
76: SAVE! Adeniran shoots from a tight angle. Sinisalo makes another save to keep the clean sheet intact.
Thank the board?
Sky Sports News' Adam Binnie was watching at Celtic Park:
What a difference a year makes.
Twelve months on from shock elimination at this stage to Kazakh club Kairat Almaty, the Scottish champions already have one foot in the league phase after the first leg.
Whisper it quietly, but the much-maligned Celtic board are due some credit.
Summer signing Camilo Duran stole the show with two outstanding goals, and fellow new recruit Mika Baur was arguably Player of the Match on his home debut. Their latest arrival Hasseim Hassan looked exciting off the bench while Kasper Hogh - though not on the scoresheet - displayed strengths in his link-up play.
The club have reinvested more than £30m on the aforementioned acquisitions and are still in the black - that's good business.
With more signings expected to land before the window shuts on September 3, and an estimated £40m to land in the club account should they progress, Celtic look in strikingly different shape than they did in Kazakhstan last August.
Curiously, there were no chants of 'sack the board' on Wednesday evening.
O'Neill: 'It's in the balance'
Celtic manager Martin O'Neill:
"I thought there were periods where we played some really fantastic stuff.
"There were also periods where they played fantastic stuff. It was really like a basketball game, particularly in the first half.
"We rode a little bit of luck. They had a great shot in the first minute, just marginally offside. They had a great chance just a moment or two after that, so they started the brighter and it took us time to get going.
"But when we did, we scored a great goal by Nygren to take a bit of pressure off, give us the lead and then Duran's two goals were fantastic.
"But, the game is absolutely in the balance yet."
McGregor: We're only halfway there
Celtic captain Callum McGregor speaking to TNT Sports:
"We are trying to get the club in the Champions League. Only halfway there but fantastic performance. We have to get finish it off next week.
On Duran: "Two unbelievable finishes, we have seen it in pre-season. He is a real threat. The thing I love about him is he is always chasing back.
"The group is good and doing well. We are always trying to work and get better. The confidence grows; it's only halfway.
Is the club going in the right direction? "It's our job to create the atmosphere and bring the happiness.
"It was important we try to strengthen. It's small steps and we have a really tough game next week."
What the result means and Celtic's next fixtures...
Celtic take a 3-0 lead to Austria for next week's second leg. Is the Champions League return on?
summary: Celtic secured a commanding 3-0 victory over LASK in the first leg of their Champions League play-off at Celtic Park. LASK had two goals disallowed for offside during a competitive match, with the second leg scheduled in Austria on Tuesday.

title: Curtis Jones on verge of leaving Liverpool for Inter Milan
author: Dominic King
content:
![Curtis Jones of Liverpool during a training session at AXA Training Centre on August 05, 2026 in Kirkby, England](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/08/19/TELEMMGLPICT000497509053_17871584715190_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqBsedz4LlBiBfB5cHH5CXna5vCmi6-QeyJelyftCLduc.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Curtis Jones of Liverpool during a training session at AXA Training Centre on August 05, 2026 in Kirkby, England](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/08/19/TELEMMGLPICT000497509053_17871584715190_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqBsedz4LlBiBfB5cHH5CXna5vCmi6-QeyJelyftCLduc.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
Curtis Jones is on the verge of ending his Liverpool career after Inter Milan returned with a £30m package that shows they want to do business.
Inter have been pursuing the England midfielder for much of 2026 but looked to have blown their chances of doing a deal earlier this summer when they offered £21m, knowing that Liverpool had a valuation of £35m.
It was their second attempt to sign Jones but once Liverpool had rejected it, it seemed likely that he would stay to see out the remaining 12 months of his contract. The Anfield club were relaxed that his deal running down would not see him lose focus.
There was an incident, though, during Liverpool’s pre-season tour of the US when Jones was involved in a row on the pitch with Dominik Szoboszlai and Kostas Tsimikas over the captaincy following a 1-0 win over Wrexham in New York.
Jones swiftly apologised for his actions, posting a statement on Instagram, but it was the kind of episode that indicated it would be better if there were a parting of ways. It is well known that he wants to join Inter and relishes the chance to move to a club where he should be a regular starter.
Inter, who have already signed fellow England players John Stones and Djed Spence this summer, contacted Liverpool on Wednesday morning with a bid €30m (£25.7m) with the potential for the fee to rise by €5m (£4.2m) in add-ons.
Liverpool have not accepted that offer but the indications are they are edging towards a situation where they will shake hands if Inter come up with a fee in line with the £35m they paid Tottenham Hotspur for Spence earlier this month.
Should the deal go through, it would be a significant departure as Jones is something of a dying breed – a young boy who grew up in Liverpool city centre, supporting the club and found his way into the first team with perseverance and talent.
He made his debut in January 2019 in an FA Cup tie at Wolves and, in total, has amassed 229 appearances and scored 22 goals – the last of which came in a 1-1 draw with Brentford on the final day of last season. He has won two Premier Leagues, the FA Cup, League Cup and Club World Cup.
Liverpool are yet to secure the right-winger they have been pursuing since Mohamed Salah left at the end of last season and – at this stage – it is unlikely they will follow up initial interest in Ibrahim Mbaye, of Paris St-Germain.
Talks for PSG’s Bradley Barcola remain ongoing, but PSG’s asking price of £120m means Liverpool are assessing alternatives if a deal cannot be done with the European champions. Levante, meanwhile, are hoping to take the highly regarded Ifeanyi Ndukwe, 18, on loan from Liverpool.
summary: Liverpool midfielder Curtis Jones is close to leaving the club for Inter Milan after Inter submitted a £30m package. Jones has long desired the move to secure regular starting minutes. Meanwhile, Liverpool continue to evaluate their options regarding wingers, including ongoing talks for Bradley Barcola.
key_points: Inter Milan made a £30m package offer for England midfielder Curtis Jones.
Jones previously had a pitch dispute with teammates during Liverpool's US pre-season tour and wants a move for regular starts.
Liverpool are nearing a potential agreement if the fee meets their £35m valuation.
Liverpool remain in ongoing talks for PSG winger Bradley Barcola amid a £120m asking price.

title: Martin O'Neill not fooled by Celtic score as he hails 'real bargain' and reveals player set for scan
author: Alan Pattullo
content:
Martin O'Neill not fooled by Celtic score as he hails 'real bargain' and reveals player set for scan
O’Neil reserves praise for several Celtic stars after 3-0 win over LASK
Celtic manager Martin O’Neill hailed his side’s performance against LASK but stressed the tie was “still in the balance” despite what sounds like a comprehensive 3-0 first-leg victory.
Three high-quality goals have put Celtic in a good position ahead of next week’s second leg in Austria. But O’Neill believes Celtic can still improve and they might have to in order to keep LASK at bay and secure the estimated £40 million windfall for clinching a return to the Champions League.
Celtic survived some shaky moments in the opening stages. LASK had a goal ruled offside and also wasted another golden chance before a bravura performance from Camilo Duran took the game away from the visitors. The Colombian struck twice after Benjamin Nygren opened the scoring on 26 minutes. “He has paid for his ticket now, it’s only his fourth game,” smiled O’Neill, referring to Duran. The forward was signed for around £6 million including add-ons from Qarabag of Azerbaijan earlier this summer. “It’s not an awful lot of money when you consider some of the fees talked about for the Premier League," noted O'Neill. "He has been a real bargain."
![Celtic's Camilo Duran celebrates after scoring to make it 3-0 over LASK in the Champions League play-off first leg at Celtic Park.  (Photo by Rob Casey / SNS Group)](https://www.scotsman.com/jpim-static/image/2026/08/19/22/29/21766947.jpg?trim=0,158,0,158&crop=&width=640&quality=65)
![placeholder image](https://www.scotsman.com/img/placeholder.jpg)
O’Neill described the opening half as “like a basketball game” with LASK passing up other good opportunities to score. “We rode our luck a little bit,” he admitted.
But having steadied themselves, Celtic took confidence from two exquisite finishes from Nygren and Duran to take a commanding 2-0 lead. Duran scored another fine goal - after exchanging passes with Nygren - midway through the second half to put Celtic in the Champions League driving seat. O’Neill, however, is taking nothing for granted.
“They (LASK) started the brighter, it took us time to get going," he said. "But when we did we scored a great goal from Nygren to take a bit of the pressure off, and give us the lead. And then Duran’s two goals were fantastic. But the game is absolutely in the balance.”
O’Neill is not fooled by the handsome first-leg lead. “I didn’t have to say it to the players in the dressing room,” he said. “They absolutely know. I think we are capable of scoring (over there) which we might need to do.
“I am not playing it down at all,” he added. “We are a long way away, genuinely. Next Tuesday will be a big test for us.
“Our goals were fantastic, good enough to win any football match,” he added. “But there is a long way to go yet.”
![Celtic's Camilo Duran (L) with Manager Martin O'Neill (R) as he is substituted during the 3-0 win over LASK in the Champions League play-off first leg at Celtic Park. (Photo by Rob Casey / SNS Group)](https://www.scotsman.com/jpim-static/image/2026/08/19/22/02/21767006.jpeg?trim=0,16,0,15&crop=&width=640&quality=65)
![placeholder image](https://www.scotsman.com/img/placeholder.jpg)
O’Neill described Duran as “exceptional”. He noted his willingness to track back to help 19-year-old right back Colby Donovan, who was also superb. “He (Duran) has been fantastic for us since he arrived at this football club,” said O’Neill. “His goals were terrific, his play was great, his running back, helping Colby out on a number of occasions. It was a magnificent performance. If he stays clear of injury, he is going to be a really, really good player.”
O’Neill also praised Nygren’s performance. The Swede has now scored in every game so far this season. “His form since the start of the season has been terrific, he was brilliant for us tonight,” said the manager.
O’Neill still believes Celtic can improve, in terms of fitness as much as anything. “We had to be at it every single minute, overall we defended strongly,” he said. “(Viljami) Sinisalo was great – he made a big save for us at 2-0. If it goes 2-1 they are in the ascendancy at that stage.”
The teenage Donovan also caught the eye at right back in front of the watching new Scotland manager Sebastien Pocognoli. “He did brilliantly, he did great,” said O’Neill. “He has a really big heart and that is nice to see. He is a local lad too and loves it, he loves the football club and loves playing. His enthusiasm is boundless and he stuck to his task brilliantly.”
Donovan is standing in for the injured Alistair Johnston, who O’Neill revealed is due to have a scan on Thursday for the leg muscle injury sustained against Kilmarnock two weekends ago. “By the time I meet up with you again, we should have an idea (how long he will be out),” he said.

Despite early scares where LASK missed several chances, goals from Benjamin Nygren and a brace from summer signing Camilo Duran secured the commanding victory. O'Neill praised Duran as a real bargain and highlighted strong performances from teenager Colby Donovan and goalkeeper Viljami Sinisalo. Additionally, the manager revealed that injured right-back Alistair Johnston is set to undergo a scan on a leg muscle injury.

title: Arsenal legend reveals why Liverpool will destroy Arteta's hopes of signing Bradley Barcola
author: Rob McCarthy
content:
![Barcola Liverpool Arsenal](https://d2x51gyc4ptf2q.cloudfront.net/content/uploads/2026/06/12123551/F365-Two-Badges-Bradley-Barcola-Arsenal-Liverpool-1320x742.jpg) 
Arsenal legend Emmanuel Petit has revealed why he believes Liverpool will ultimately beat the reigning Premier League champions to the signing of Bradley Barcola this summer, with a deal set to cost well in excess of £100million.
Both clubs remain on the hunt for a new wide player before the window closes on September 1, with exciting PSG and France star Barcola on the radars of the two English powerhouses.
Liverpool have long been considered the frontrunners to sign Barcola, with the 23-year-old poised to leave the French giants due to negotiations over a new contract having stalled.
While Barcola is understood to be keen on a move to Anfield and personal terms have already been agreed, FSG are currently reluctant to meet PSG’s £130million (€151m) asking price.
Arsenal, for their part, have been a little later in showing their interest in Barcola, but are being linked after offloading Leandro Trossard and also preparing to part ways with Gabriel Martinelli.
Petit, however, believes Barcola would be best served by a move to Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool, especially given the impressive start Christos Tzolis has made at Arsenal since summer switch from Club Brugge.
“Arsenal have just signed Christos Tzolis, who has made a big impression so far, he was brilliant in the Community Shield,” Petit told Grosvenor Sport.
“With Martinelli leaving and Trossard no longer at the club, they likely need another option on the left side.
“If they were to bring in Barcola, it would be difficult for both players to secure a spot in the starting eleven.
“That said, I am a huge fan of Barcola. I believe Liverpool need him much more than Arsenal.
“They definitely need to strengthen their wide areas, particularly on the left flank, they have had problems there since the start of last season.”
Petit struggling to see Liverpool in top four
Meanwhile, Petit believes that even if Liverpool win the race to snap up Barcola, Iraola still faces an uphill task to secure the club a top-four finish this season.
The Spaniard swapped Bournemouth for the Merseyside giants following Arne Slot’s exit at the end of last season, but Petit thinks the Reds currently have too many holes in their squad to compete with a top-four spot.
The Frenchman added: “I am still waiting to see Liverpool’s full intent in the transfer market, as they currently appear to be missing key players.
“They have a new manager in Iraola, and adjusting to the scale of Liverpool after Bournemouth is a big transition.
“Liverpool need results immediately.
“Ultimately, I see the top four being Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester City, and Manchester United. Liverpool may find it tough again this year.”
summary: Arsenal legend Emmanuel Petit believes Liverpool will win the race to sign PSG winger Bradley Barcola for over £100 million because they need him more than Arsenal, who recently signed Christos Tzolis. While personal terms are reportedly agreed with Liverpool, FSG is currently hesitant to meet PSG's £130 million valuation. Despite predicting Barcola will choose Liverpool, Petit remains doubtful that the club—now managed by Andoni Iraola following Arne Slot's departure—will finish in the Premier League top four.
key_points: Both Arsenal and Liverpool are pursuing PSG and France winger Bradley Barcola, with a potential deal expected to exceed £100 million.
Barcola has already agreed personal terms with Liverpool, but FSG is reluctant to meet PSG's £130 million asking price.
Emmanuel Petit believes Barcola is better suited to Liverpool because Arsenal recently signed Christos Tzolis, creating potential competition for the starting eleven.
Petit predicts that Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester City, and Manchester United will make the top four, leaving Liverpool struggling under new manager Andoni Iraola.

title: Nick Kyrgios: Controversial tennis player's career could be over after positive cocaine test
author: Russell Fuller
content:
![Nick Kyrgios gestures after a point in the Wimbledon men's singles final in 2022](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/71a2/live/4841ebf0-9be2-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.jpg)
Nick Kyrgios has won seven ATP Tour singles titles
- Published
Nick Kyrgios once said there was "zero chance" he would be playing tennis into his 30s.
But it was at the age of 31, while attempting another comeback from serious knee and wrist injuries, that he tested positive for a metabolite of cocaine at June's Mallorca Open.
In a post on social media, Kyrgios said it was a "huge mistake" for which he takes full responsibility.
But he added that recent injuries - he has only played eight tournaments and won two matches since the start of 2023 - have taken a huge toll on him.
"Coming to terms with being near the end of my career has been harder than I ever imagined," he added.
Kyrgios will not be able to play until his case is resolved because of a mandatory provisional suspension.
But although he faces a potential ban of up to four years, his suspension would be limited to a maximum of three months if he can prove the drug was taken out of competition.
Kyrgios suspended after positive cocaine test
The Australian has achieved more than most on the sporting stage. As a 19-year-old in 2014 he stunned then world number one Rafael Nadal on his Centre Court debut, and finished runner-up at Wimbledon eight years later.
At his best, Kyrgios is a flamboyant and athletic shot-maker with flair, touch and an explosive game.
But he can also be destructive and verbally abusive, and has regularly struggled to sustain the levels of professionalism and abstinence needed for a prolonged stay at the very top.
In 2015, Kyrgios was given a suspended 28-day ban for making lewd remarks about Stan Wawrinka's girlfriend during a match in Montreal.
A year later, he was banned for eight weeks for his behaviour - including a "lack of best effort" - at the Shanghai Masters. This was reduced to three weeks after he agreed to consult a sports psychologist.
2019 was the nadir. Kyrgios was defaulted from a match at the Italian Open for hurling a chair on to the court, and was later fined $113,000 for verbally abusing umpire Fergus Murphy in Cincinnati.
The ATP later issued a suspended 16-week ban for a "pattern of behaviour related to his verbal abuse of officials and/or spectators" over the previous 12 months.
![Nick Kyrgios walks off with the Wimbledon singles runner-up trophy after losing the 2022 final to Novak Djokovic](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/a2d0/live/08e2d5b0-9bdc-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
Nick Kyrgios reached his sole Grand Slam singles final at Wimbledon in 2022, losing to Novak Djokovic
Kyrgios described 2019 as the "lowest point of my career" when interviewed for Netflix's Break Point documentary series.
"I was drinking, abusing drugs. I lost my relationship with my family, pushed all my close friends away," he said.
"Being bullied at a young age for being short and fat and brown scarred me for sure."
Kyrgios said he wore a compression sleeve to cover up self-harming scars on his arm and spent time in a psychiatric hospital in London to try and "figure out my problems".
He separately spoke about being forced out of a pub in Wimbledon Village by his agent in the early hours of a match day, and told Louis Theroux in 2024 that he would sometimes have "20 to 30 drinks" before playing the next day.
He has confessed to playing too much basketball - including for an hour before he beat David Ferrer in the 2017 Cincinnati Masters semi-finals - and has often said he has been unable to "dedicate" his life to tennis.
"I just enjoy doing whatever I'm doing," he said.
"I don't eat well. I don't train just for tennis, I train just for a general happy living - I know it sounds ridiculous, but I play a bit of tennis on the side."
![Nick Kyrgios and Thanasi Kokkinakis pose after winning the Australian Open men's doubles title in 2022](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/b347/live/3bdbd890-9bdc-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
Nick Kyrgios (right) and good friend Thanasi Kokkinakis won the Australian Open men's doubles title in 2022
In 2023, Kyrgios admitted assaulting ex-girlfriend Chiara Passari by pushing her on the pavement during a row in Canberra. The magistrate called the incident "a single act of stupidity or frustration" when sparing him a criminal record.
Then two years ago he publicly distanced himself from controversial influencer Andrew Tate, who is currently fighting extradition to the UK on charges including rape and offences related to sex trafficking.
Kyrgios told the BBC he had "deleted posts, unfollowed him and gone to all lengths to distance" himself from Tate.
The current world number 919 will now step away from public life for the next 28 days to "do the work and come back better".
The legal process could take many months - and Kyrgios is no fan of tennis' anti-doping system.
Describing the system as "awful," he made clear repeatedly his opinion that both Jannik Sinner and Iga Swiatek received overly lenient bans after their recent high-profile doping cases.
"Sad day for tennis. Fairness in tennis does not exist," Kyrgios wrote after Sinner accepted a three-month ban for testing positive for clostebol.
But if he does decide he wants to continue his career into his 30s, much will rest on the process of which Kyrgios has been so critical.
If you, or someone you know, have been affected by any issues raised in this article, support and information is available at BBC Action Line. You can also contact the Samaritans on a free helpline at 116 123, or visit the website., external
summary: Tennis player Nick Kyrgios is facing a potential ban of up to four years after testing positive for a cocaine metabolite at the Mallorca Open. Kyrgios, who is currently 31 and attempting a comeback from serious injuries, acknowledged the positive test as a "huge mistake" while admitting that coming to terms with the end of his career has been extremely difficult. He is currently serving a mandatory provisional suspension while the legal process is resolved.

He faces a mandatory provisional suspension and a potential ban of up to four years, though it could be limited to three months if he proves the drug was taken out of competition.
Kyrgios stated that coming to terms with the end of his career has been harder than he imagined, following a series of serious knee and wrist injuries.
The Australian player has a history of controversies, disciplinary issues, and struggles with mental health and substance abuse throughout his career.

title: Arsenal agree £51m deal to sign Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa
author: Jamie Jackson; David Hytner; Ben Fisher
content:
Arsenal have agreed a £51 million (€59.5 million) deal to sign Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa. The Premier League champions have been keen to find defensive cover for William Saliba and Jurriën Timber, who are out with injuries. They have tracked Konsa throughout the summer and have made a breakthrough in the negotiations.
Mikel Arteta hopes Konsa, whose Villa contract has two years to run, can make light of Saliba’s absence in central defence. The time frame for the Frenchman’s return is unclear but he is not expected to play before mid-October, having sustained a back injury in France’s World Cup semi-final defeat against Spain. Konsa’s appeal is bolstered by the fact he can also play at right-back, where Timber is battling to return from a groin injury which has affected him for months.
Konsa starred for England on their run to the World Cup semi-finals. A fixture in Villa’s successful team, the 28-year-old will encounter fierce competition at Arsenal, especially when Saliba is fit. Arteta rates Saliba’s partnership with Gabriel Magalhães as the best in England but he thinks the addition of a player of Konsa’s calibre is a signal of Arsenal’s desire to build on their title success of last season and dominate.
The manager knows that his team played 63 matches in all competitions last season, which included runs to the Champions League and Carabao Cup finals, and he hopes to have a similar number this time out. As such, he believes he will be able to give Konsa the minutes he would expect, particularly when injuries are factored in. Arteta is also determined to have more high-quality options so that he can better rotate. At present, he has eight defenders, including Myles Lewis-Skelly, who can play in midfield.
READ MORE
Konsa joined Villa from Brentford in 2019 and has been central to their rise up the Premier League table under Unai Emery. He has made 286 appearances for them and was a part of the team that won the Europa League last season. Arsenal kick off the new season at home to Coventry on Friday night.
![Al-Hilal are pursuing a move for Ollie Watkins. Photograph: Nigel French/PA](https://www.irishtimes.com/resizer/v2/SXY7NENEZ75SX45WVJQF225XSM.jpg?auth=4948b8ee1333763a29fd40561c6cf76a6ff4b0c664f2655d914cc9d343b60cdf&width=800&height=533)
Villa are also braced for another bid from Al-Hilal for Ollie Watkins, after rejecting an offer worth almost £40 million (€46.7 million) for the striker. Al-Hilal are pursuing a move for Villa’s all-time Premier League goalscorer, who has reached double figures in the top flight in his six seasons at the club after joining from Brentford.
If Villa sell Watkins, who has two years on his contract, they would seek to replace the 30-year-old England striker and Emery is a big admirer of Nicolas Jackson, but Chelsea’s valuation of £65 million (€75.8 million) is thought to be prohibitive to any deal. There is an acceptance at Villa that any marquee arrival before the close of the window would probably have to follow another major sale, owing to the Premier League’s financial regulations.
Emery has had to significantly reshape his squad this summer after the departures of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, who joined Chelsea, Manchester United and Paris Saint-Germain respectively, with Konsa now also on the move.
Villa have signed Zion Suzuki as a replacement for Emiliano Martínez, whose future remains unclear. Suzuki, a £30 million (€35 million) buy from Parma, will be the first Japanese goalkeeper to play in the Premier League.
Villa have completed the £17 million (€19.8 million) signing of Matteo Ruggeri from Atlético Madrid and remain in talks with Bayern Munich over a deal for João Palhinha and West Ham for Aaron Wan-Bissaka. Villa have also signed Johan Manzambi from Freiburg for a club-record £52 million (€60.6 million) and João Gomes from Wolves for £38 million (€44.3 million). There could be further sales, with Villa hoping to find Martínez a new club.
Villa gave Watkins, together with Martínez and Konsa, an extended four-week break after the World Cup. Emery said Watkins volunteered to play in last week’s Super Cup against PSG, but the manager advised him to continue to rest.
![Carlos Baleba would be United’s third midfielder recruit of the summer. Photograph: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images](https://www.irishtimes.com/resizer/v2/ILX65ZPV7FB6TIHR6MGRXJIGJM.jpg?auth=b14742396f3aaa913b22f61b53558a2985826bce6f73c6bf615ad124f36f9699&width=800&height=533)
Meanwhile, Manchester United are confident of signing Brighton’s Carlos Baleba for less than £75 million (€87.6 million), with the 22-year-old midfielder having agreed personal terms. United have made an initial offer of £60 million (€70.1 million) plus £5 million (€5.8 million) add-ons for Baleba, which is below Brighton’s valuation.
Baleba has been a target for United since last summer, when Brighton valued him at about £100 million (€116.8 million). The Cameroon international’s price has dropped after his largely uneven performances last season.
Baleba, who has an ankle injury, would be United’s third midfielder recruit of the summer, after Youri Tielemans, who was signed for £35 million (€40.9 million) from Aston Villa, and Andrey Santos, who arrived for £48 million (€56 million) from Chelsea.
Baleba, whose preference is to play as a No 6, would add dynamism and energy to United’s engine room, and compete with Santos for a starting berth.
United, whose opening Premier League fixture is at Hull on Saturday, remain in the market for a left-back. Newcastle’s Lewis Hall and Arsenal’s Myles Lewis-Skelly are high on the list of candidates. – Guardian
summary: Arsenal have agreed a £51 million deal to sign defender Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa to provide cover for the injured William Saliba and Jurriën Timber. Konsa, who starred for England at the World Cup, will add valuable depth and rotation options for Mikel Arteta's squad. Meanwhile, Aston Villa are preparing for potential further squad changes and interest in striker Ollie Watkins.
key_points: Arsenal reached a £51 million agreement with Aston Villa for Ezri Konsa.
Konsa provides defensive cover for injured center-back William Saliba and right-back Jurriën Timber.
Aston Villa previously rejected a nearly £40 million bid from Al-Hilal for striker Ollie Watkins.
Manchester United have made an initial offer of £60 million plus add-ons for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba.

The timeframe for the Frenchman’s return is unclear but he is not expected to play before mid-October, having sustained a back injuryin France’s World Cup semi-final defeat against Spain.
Konsa’s appeal is bolstered by the fact he can also play at right-back, where Timber is battling to return from a groin injury which has affected him for months.
Konsa starred for England on their run to the World Cup semi-finals. A fixture in Villa’s successful team, the 28-year-old will encounter fierce competition at Arsenal, especially when Saliba is fit. Arteta rates Saliba’s partnership with Gabriel Magalhães as the best in England but he thinks the addition of a player of Konsa’s calibre is a signal of Arsenal’s desire to build on their title success of last season and dominate.
The manager knows that his team played 63 matches in all competitions last season, which included runs to the Champions League and Carabao Cup finals, and he hopes to have a similar number this time out. As such, he believes he will be able to give Konsa the minutes he would expect, particularly when injuries are factored in. Arteta is also determined to have more high-quality options so that he can better rotate. At present, he has eight defenders, including Myles Lewis-Skelly, who can play in midfield.
Konsa joined Villa from Brentford in 2019 and has been central to their rise under Unai Emery. He has made 286 appearances for them and was a part of the team that won the Europa League last season. Arsenal kick off the new season at home to Coventry on Friday night.
Meanwhile, Villa are braced for another bid from Al-Hilal for Ollie Watkins, after rejecting an offer worth almost £40m for the striker. Al-Hilal are pursuing a move for Villa’s all-time Premier League goalscorer, who has reached double figures in the top flight in his six seasons at the club after joining from Brentford.
If Villa sell Watkins, who has two years on his contract, they would seek to replace the 30-year-old England striker and Emery is a big admirer of Nicolas Jackson, but Chelsea’s valuation of £65m is thought to be prohibitive to any deal. There is an acceptance at Villa that any marquee arrival before the close of the window would probably have to follow another major sale, owing to the Premier League’s financial regulations.
Emery has had to significantly reshape his squad this summer after the departures of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, who joined Chelsea, Manchester United and Paris Saint-Germain respectively, with Konsa now also on the move.
Villa have signed Zion Suzuki as a replacement for Emiliano Martínez, whose future remains unclear. Suzuki, a £30m buy from Parma, will be the first Japanese goalkeeper to play in the Premier League.
Villa have completed the £17m signing of Matteo Ruggeri from Atlético Madrid and remain in talks with Bayern Munich over a deal for João Palhinha and West Ham for Aaron Wan-Bissaka. Villa have also signed Johan Manzambi from Freiburg for a club-record £52m and João Gomes from Wolves for £38m. There could be further sales, with Villa hoping to find Martínez a new club.
Villa gave Watkins, together with Konsa, an extended four-week break after the World Cup. Emery said Watkins volunteered to play in last week’s Super Cup against PSG, but the manager advised him to continue to rest.
summary: Arsenal have agreed to a £51m deal with Aston Villa to sign defender Ezri Konsa to provide cover for injured players like William Saliba and Jurriën Timber. The 28-year-old England international can play centrally and at right-back, bringing added depth to Mikel Arteta's squad. Meanwhile, Aston Villa face potential further squad changes, including handling interest in Ollie Watkins from Al-Hilal and reshaping their team following several key departures.
key_points: Arsenal agreed a £51m fee with Aston Villa for the transfer of Ezri Konsa.
Konsa provides defensive cover for injured players William Saliba and Jurriën Timber.
Aston Villa rejected a nearly £40m bid from Al-Hilal for striker Ollie Watkins.
Aston Villa have experienced several squad changes this summer, including the departures of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, and Lucas Digne.

title: Nick Kyrgios: Controversial tennis player's career could be over after positive cocaine test
author: Russell Fuller
content:
![Nick Kyrgios gestures after a point in the Wimbledon men's singles final in 2022](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/71a2/live/4841ebf0-9be2-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.jpg)
Nick Kyrgios has won seven ATP Tour singles titles
- Published
Nick Kyrgios once said there was "zero chance" he would be playing tennis into his 30s.
But it was at the age of 31, while attempting another comeback from serious knee and wrist injuries, that he tested positive for a metabolite of cocaine at June's Mallorca Open.
In a post on social media, Kyrgios said it was a "huge mistake" for which he takes full responsibility.
But he added that recent injuries - he has only played eight tournaments and won two matches since the start of 2023 - have taken a huge toll on him.
"Coming to terms with being near the end of my career has been harder than I ever imagined," he added.
Kyrgios will not be able to play until his case is resolved because of a mandatory provisional suspension.
But although he faces a potential ban of up to four years, his suspension would be limited to a maximum of three months if he can prove the drug was taken out of competition.
Kyrgios suspended after positive cocaine test
The Australian has achieved more than most on the sporting stage. As a 19-year-old in 2014 he stunned then world number one Rafael Nadal on his Centre Court debut, and finished runner-up at Wimbledon eight years later.
At his best, Kyrgios is a flamboyant and athletic shot-maker with flair, touch and an explosive game.
But he can also be destructive and verbally abusive, and has regularly struggled to sustain the levels of professionalism and abstinence needed for a prolonged stay at the very top.
In 2015, Kyrgios was given a suspended 28-day ban for making lewd remarks about Stan Wawrinka's girlfriend during a match in Montreal.
A year later, he was banned for eight weeks for his behaviour - including a "lack of best effort" - at the Shanghai Masters. This was reduced to three weeks after he agreed to consult a sports psychologist.
2019 was the nadir. Kyrgios was defaulted from a match at the Italian Open for hurling a chair on to the court, and was later fined $113,000 for verbally abusing umpire Fergus Murphy in Cincinnati.
The ATP later issued a suspended 16-week ban for a "pattern of behaviour related to his verbal abuse of officials and/or spectators" over the previous 12 months.
![Nick Kyrgios walks off with the Wimbledon singles runner-up trophy after losing the 2022 final to Novak Djokovic](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/a2d0/live/08e2d5b0-9bdc-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
Nick Kyrgios reached his sole Grand Slam singles final at Wimbledon in 2022, losing to Novak Djokovic
Kyrgios described 2019 as the "lowest point of my career" when interviewed for Netflix's Break Point documentary series.
"I was drinking, abusing drugs. I lost my relationship with my family, pushed all my close friends away," he said.
"Being bullied at a young age for being short and fat and brown scarred me for sure."
Kyrgios said he wore a compression sleeve to cover up self-harming scars on his arm and spent time in a psychiatric hospital in London to try and "figure out my problems".
He separately spoke about being forced out of a pub in Wimbledon Village by his agent in the early hours of a match day, and told Louis Theroux in 2024 that he would sometimes have "20 to 30 drinks" before playing the next day.
He has confessed to playing too much basketball - including for an hour before he beat David Ferrer in the 2017 Cincinnati Masters semi-finals - and has often said he has been unable to "dedicate" his life to tennis.
"I just enjoy doing whatever I'm doing," he said.
"I don't eat well. I don't train just for tennis, I train just for a general happy living - I know it sounds ridiculous, but I play a bit of tennis on the side."
![Nick Kyrgios and Thanasi Kokkinakis pose after winning the Australian Open men's doubles title in 2022](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/b347/live/3bdbd890-9bdc-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
Nick Kyrgios (right) and good friend Thanasi Kokkinakis won the Australian Open men's doubles title in 2022
In 2023, Kyrgios admitted assaulting ex-girlfriend Chiara Passari by pushing her on the pavement during a row in Canberra. The magistrate called the incident "a single act of stupidity or frustration" when sparing him a criminal record.
Then two years ago he publicly distanced himself from controversial influencer Andrew Tate, who is currently fighting extradition to the UK on charges including rape and offences related to sex trafficking.
Kyrgios told the BBC he had "deleted posts, unfollowed him and gone to all lengths to distance" himself from Tate.
The current world number 919 will now step away from public life for the next 28 days to "do the work and come back better".
The legal process could take many months - and Kyrgios is no fan of tennis' anti-doping system.
Describing the system as "awful," he made clear repeatedly his opinion that both Jannik Sinner and Iga Swiatek received overly lenient bans after their recent high-profile doping cases.
"Sad day for tennis. Fairness in tennis does not exist," Kyrgios wrote after Sinner accepted a three-month ban for testing positive for clostebol.
But if he does decide he wants to continue his career into his 30s, much will rest on the process of which Kyrgios has been so critical.
If you, or someone you know, have been affected by any issues raised in this article, support and information is available at BBC Action Line. You can also contact the Samaritans on a free helpline at 116 123, or visit the website., external
summary: Australian tennis player Nick Kyrgios faces a mandatory provisional suspension and potential career end after testing positive for a metabolite of cocaine at the Mallorca Open. Kyrgios acknowledged the mistake and took full responsibility, noting that coping with recent injuries and nearing the end of his career has been extremely difficult. Throughout his career, Kyrgios has achieved notable successes, including winning seven ATP singles titles and reaching the 2022 Wimbledon final, alongside a history of disciplinary issues and personal struggles.
key_points: Nick Kyrgios tested positive for a cocaine metabolite at the Mallorca Open at age 31 while attempting a comeback from knee and wrist injuries.
He faces a mandatory provisional suspension pending the resolution of his case, with a potential ban of up to four years.
Kyrgios admitted the positive test was a "huge mistake" and stated that coming to terms with the end of his career has been very hard.

His career features notable athletic achievements, such as reaching the 2022 Wimbledon singles final and winning the 2022 Australian Open doubles title, alongside a well-documented history of fines, bans, and personal controversies.

The weight of history is against Arsenal defending their trophy, however. Arsenal have not defended the top-flight title since the 1930s. It is another milestone Arteta is keen to overcome.
"That's an opportunity that we have ahead, and we are very conscious of what it's going to take to deliver that," he said. "But I feel the ambition, I feel the desire, and I feel the ability and the conviction around the team that we can do it."
